candidates.description: The current password check on line 39 is guarded by `if (currentPassword && ...)`, so when `currentPassword` is an empty string, undefined, or null, the entire verification is skipped and the password is changed without proof of the current one.
candidates.rationale: Line 39 uses short-circuit evaluation: if `currentPassword` is falsy the hash comparison never executes. Line 51 then writes the new password unconditionally. An authenticated user can POST with `current=` (empty) to change their password without knowing the old one. Verification: send a change-password request with an empty `current` query param using a valid token and confirm the password is updated.
candidates.title: Current password verification bypassed when parameter is falsy

candidates.description: Line 51 stores `newPasswordInString` (the raw query parameter) directly into the user record, while line 39 expects the stored value to be a hash. After a successful change the password is persisted unhashed.
candidates.rationale: `newPasswordInString` is `newPassword?.toString()` with no hashing applied. Line 39 compares `security.hash(currentPassword)` against the stored value, proving the schema expects a hash. The challenge check on line 54 further confirms hashed storage is the norm. Verification: change a password, then read the user record via an admin or data-export endpoint and confirm the password field is the plain-text value.
candidates.title: New password stored in plain text without hashing

candidates.description: Lines 29-33 iterate over user-supplied field names and copy matching keys from `user.data` into the response without an allowlist, allowing extraction of sensitive fields such as the password hash.
candidates.rationale: The loop on line 29 checks only `user?.data[field] !== undefined` before including the value. No allowlist restricts which keys may be returned. Line 52 explicitly solves a challenge when `response.user.password` is present, confirming the password field is reachable through this path. Verification: request `/rest/user/whoami?fields=password` with a valid token and confirm the hash appears in the JSON response.
candidates.title: Arbitrary user-data field exposure via fields query parameter

candidates.description: Line 26 inserts `req.body.author` directly into the review document without verifying it matches the authenticated user's email, allowing any authenticated user to post reviews attributed to another identity.
candidates.rationale: The `author` value is taken verbatim from the request body. The only related check (line 19) is a challenge-solve condition, not an enforcement gate. No middleware or handler rejects a mismatch between `user.data.email` and `req.body.author`. Verification: authenticate as user A, POST a review with `author` set to user B's email, and confirm the review is stored with the forged author.
candidates.title: Review author field not validated against authenticated user identity
